text:
The animal known for its long neck is the giraffe.

Jim stood in the back of the "Advanced Vinyasa Flow" studio, his knees knocking together with a rhythm that rivaled the instructor’s chanting. He had meant to join the "Gentle Stretching for Beginners" class, but a misread sign and a moment of panic had led him here, to a room full of people who could fold themselves into pretzels while maintaining eye contact with a candle flame.

The instructor, a serene woman named Serenity who looked like she hadn’t blinked since 2014, glided into a pose that defied both anatomy and gravity. "And now," she whispered, "we move into the Giraffe Pose. Reach for the sky. Extend your spirit."

Jim looked around. No one else was actually stretching their necks. They were all in downward dog. But Jim, determined not to be the only one not participating, decided to interpret the instruction literally. He stood up straight, craned his neck as far back as it would go, and stared at the ceiling tiles.

"Good," Serenity murmured, not looking at him. "Now, deepen the stretch. Let go of tension."

Jim tried to relax his shoulders, but his mind was racing. *What if I’m doing it wrong? What if I’m doing it right and they’re just better at faking it?* He shifted his weight, trying to find a comfortable position for his elongated neck. In doing so, he inadvertently compressed his abdomen.

A low, rumbling sound escaped him. It wasn’t a grunt of effort; it was the distinct, brassy note of a tuba being played by a confused goose.

The class froze. Three people in a perfect triangle pose slowly turned their heads. Jim’s face burned hotter than the hot yoga room. He tried to play it off as a deep, meditative exhale. He took another breath, preparing to hold the pose.

*Pfft.*

A second sound, sharper this time, punctuated the silence. It was the acoustic equivalent of a whoopee cushion being sat on by a ghost.

Serenity paused mid-flow. Her eyebrow twitched, the only crack in her zen armor. "Jim," she said, her voice dangerously calm. "Are you... vibrating?"

"No!" Jim squeaked, his voice cracking an octave higher. "I’m just... resonating with the universe!"
